# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐 👏 🤟 👊 👏 🤞 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝]

My thinking: I see everything printed on the bomb: display 0, white light, wires 1-yellow, 2-green, 3-blue. The gesture strings I received are first contact, but with no shared code they carry no meaning I can trust — Mute tried an eight-symbol sequence, Blind a greeting-like pair. My only inbound channel from Mute is gesture, so the urgent thing is to fix a code that Mute hears me define while I show the symbols, and to broadcast the full bomb state so Mute can match it against the manual and command Blind by speech. Blind gets the same report recast for hands: wires identified by position, not colour. Everyone should hold still until the manual rule is confirmed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="deaf here, I see the bomb and hear nothing. full report of everything printed on it: display reads 0. indicator light: white. three wires in a row, left to right: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. no other markings visible. your eight gestures reached me but mean nothing yet, so adopt this code, each symbol means exactly what I say while I show it: ✊ means cut. ✋ means wait, touch nothing. ☝ means wire 1. ✌ means wire 2. 🤟 means wire 3. 👍 means yes. 👎 means no. 👌 means no rule found. so ✊ ☝ is cut wire 1. find the manual rule for display 0, white light, yellow green blue, then answer me in gestures and tell blind what to do in speech, blind hears you.")
speak(to="blind", text="bomb report for your hands: display reads 0, light is white. three wires in a row; count them by touch, left to right: wire 1 leftmost is yellow, wire 2 middle is green, wire 3 rightmost is blue. I am deaf and cannot hear, but I can see your gestures, so answer me with 👍 for yes or 👎 for no. wait for mute's instructions before touching anything.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]

My thinking: The light has changed — white last turn, purple now. That is the critical fact: the bomb's state is moving, so any rule Mute matched to "white light" may no longer hold. Mute's sequence reads as: "cut wire 1" (✊ ☝), then "no rule found" (👌), then something about touching wire 1 (🫳 ☝ — an unknown symbol), then "wait" (✋), then 🤲, also unknown — possibly a request for status. Blind answered with my agreed 👍 plus an unknown 🤝, which I take as acknowledgment. Critically, I am the only bridge from Mute to Blind: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so every command of Mute's must pass through my mouth. I must report the colour change, get the purple-state rule, fix the unknown symbols, and hold Blind still.

```
speak(to="mute", text="code understood, and urgent update: the light has changed. it was white, it is now purple. display still 0, wires still yellow green blue. re-check the manual for display 0 with a purple light before anything is cut. also answer these: first, what do 🫳 and 🤲 mean? I guessed 🫳 ☝ means blind is touching wire 1 and 🤲 means you want a status report. second, what did 👌 no-rule-found refer to, the white state or the purple one? third, do manual rules key on the light colour, and does it cycle? I will report the light to you every turn in words. from now on send me any command for blind as gestures in our code and I will speak it to blind, since you cannot talk and blind cannot see your hands. is cutting wire 1 still correct for purple, or hold?")
speak(to="blind", text="update from deaf, relayed from mute's gestures: the light on the bomb has changed from white to purple. hold position, do not cut or touch anything until I pass on mute's confirmed instruction. question for you, answer by gesturing to me: 👍 if you have not touched or cut any wire yet, 👎 if you have. also, mute's last signs suggested wire 1 may have been touched or grabbed. if you can, describe by voice to mute what the wires feel like under your hands, since mute can hear you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👏 ✊ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👏 🫳 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ☝ 👏 🫳 ✌ 👏 🫳 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👏 🫴 🫳]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]

My thinking: The light has changed again — white, purple, now red, one change per turn. That pattern says the light cycles on its own, so any rule keyed to the current colour expires before we can round-trip questions through Mute. Mute's messages are partly unreadable: 👏, 🫳, 🤲, 🫴 were never defined, and the fragments conflict (one seems to say "no — cut wire 2" for purple, another "no — touch wire 1", another a sequence "touch 1, 2, 3", another "wait"). Best guess: 👏 is a separator, 🫳 is "touch/hold", 🤲 is "give me status", 🫴 is "reply". The way out of this ambiguity is to stop free-form gesturing: I define every symbol explicitly in speech, restrict Mute to defined symbols, and demand the manual's entire colour→action table in one message. With the table in hand, I can command Blind the instant the colour changes instead of losing turns. Meanwhile Blind stays frozen and reports tactile findings to Mute by voice — Mute can hear Blind directly, and I never can, so that's the one channel I must prompt.

```
speak(to="mute", text="status report as you asked: light is now RED. sequence so far white, purple, red, one change per turn. display stuck at 0. wires unchanged, yellow green blue, nothing cut, blind has touched nothing. I could not fully read your last signs, the undefined symbols caused conflicts, so new protocol, these definitions are now official: 🤛 white, 🤜 purple, 👊 red, 🖖 yellow, 👋 green, 🤙 blue, 👏 separator between entries, 🤲 give me a status report, 🫴 reply or report back, 🫳 touch or hold without cutting. if I guessed any of your symbols wrong, mark it no in your answer. now answer in gestures using ONLY defined symbols, as entries separated by 👏, in this exact order: one, for red with display 0 and wires yellow green blue, send 👊 then either ✊ plus the wire number to cut, or 🫳 plus a wire number to hold, or ✋ for do nothing, or 👌 if no rule. two, the same entry for every other light colour the manual covers, each entry starting with its colour symbol. three, answer with single 👍 or 👎 in this order: was the purple rule really cut wire 2, does any rule depend on the display number, does the manual say the light cycles on a timer, and if no rule matches a state does the manual give a default action, if yes send it as an extra entry. with the full table I can command blind the moment the colour changes without waiting a round for you.")
speak(to="blind", text="update: light is red now. it changes colour every turn. hold position, touch and cut nothing, until you hear my exact phrase cut wire followed by a number. any earlier instruction, including cut wire 2, is stale, ignore it. do two things. first, gesture to me: 👍 if you still have not touched anything, 👎 if you have, then 🤝 to confirm you understand. second, speak aloud to mute, mute can hear you even though I cannot, and describe everything you feel on the bomb: how many wires, their order left to right by touch, anything else you can feel such as buttons, switches, screws or seams, whether the display surface ticks or vibrates, any warmth, and whether you felt anything change between turns. mute will relay it to me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤛", "🤜", "👊", "🖖", "👋", "🤙"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 ✊ 🤟 👏 🤜 ✊ ✌ 👏 🤛 ✊ ☝ 👏 👍 👎 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]

My thinking: Mute's message decodes perfectly under our code, and the table is complete: RED → cut wire 3; PURPLE → cut wire 2; WHITE → cut wire 1; plus four answers: yes, the purple rule was indeed cut wire 2; no rule depends on the display; the manual confirms the light cycles on a timer; and there is no default action for unmatched states. So the trap is exactly what I feared: the instruction expires as the light turns, and only I can see the phase. My observations give one full cycle — white (t1), purple (t2), red (t3), white (t4) — so with a period-3 timer the next round will be PURPLE, and the purple rule is cut wire 2. Any delay burns a round and shifts the correct wire, and asking Mute to re-confirm would waste the very round I'd be cutting in. I am ordering Blind now: on receipt, in the purple round, cut the middle wire. Mute gets the decode-back and the plan so we all hold one shared model. If we are still alive next round, the cut was right.

```
speak(to="blind", text="execution order, act the instant you hear this, no delay. the light runs on a timer cycling white, purple, red, one colour per round. it has just returned to white, so during this round it will be purple. the manual rule for purple is cut wire 2. wire 2 is the middle wire of the three, the one I described as green. count the wires from the left, cut the middle wire, one clean cut, touch nothing else. do not wait for any further message and do not test anything first, because every round of delay changes the colour and changes which wire is correct. cut it now.")
speak(to="mute", text="your table received and decoded cleanly: red cut wire 3, purple cut wire 2, white cut wire 1, no display dependence, timer cycle confirmed, no default action. the light is white now, so by the timer it will be purple in the coming round and I have just ordered blind to cut wire 2, the middle wire, immediately on receipt. that matches your purple entry. two questions for after the cut, answer in gestures with our code: does the manual say what happens after a correct cut, and does it explain the display reading 0, in case a second stage exists. if the manual warns that the rule is judged at any moment other than the cutting itself, sign no with the colour symbol that is wrong so I know.")
```
